body: my taste is so sick. I've literally spent 27 years experiencing as much life as anyone on the planet. I have to have conviction in what I think is interesting and worth my time. My nature is to be apologetic about my interests but the central tenant of 3.0 may be to do away with that. Less bothered by public opinion and other's feelings towards me. I like esports and folk music and basketball podcasts and books about the occult. I like David Bowie and cowboy bebop and sprawling video essays. I like black coffee and industrial albums and petting a dog at the bike repair shop. I love my city and my family and my closest friends so dearly (I have little trouble with my conviction on this front). I dislike repeating words within a paragraph and celebrity gossip and making plans. I dislike Joel Embiid and talking to strangers and having an appointment later in the day that I have to think about all day. I love the feeling of weightlessness that strikes me when I'm wholly content, that feeling of floating above at all, eyes on the horizon, an irrepressible smile and a song that fills my head to match the feeling. My gratitude is boundless in those moments and and is fleeting all the same. Perspective is everything. Writing is a surgical extraction of the hedges making my mind a maze. I can feel it on the bridge of my nose when It is happening, I think I should switch to poems in this state.

title: listless
body: Listless does not mean without a list. The etymology is more like lustless, lacking passion or desire. So no, I'm not lustless or listless, I'm list-less. I have no list, ordered or step-by-step, bucket or otherwise. No dots to connect, no rails to stay on. I guess I have principles and more vague 'north-stars' that dictate my behavior. One thing I certainly have is desire and passion. I ache when the latent energy of youth hisses from the seams of my form. I want to do, but I often think. Sitting down to write has been a challenge recently, posting is even harder. But realistically the roadblock that keeps me from propelling myself forward with this potential energy is fear. Fear that my peers will see my endeavors as foolish or arbitrary. That my expression will be too artsy and weird- or too samey and plain. I fear that my writing form is indiscernible, that I lack structure to convey my ideas effectively. No brevity, no second pass, just a train of thought. A list provides some shelter from the fear. So I'm going to try and make a list. Two lists actually. Feebs 3.0, and a things I really want to do but I am slightly scared to do list. Actually, on the recommendation of my friend, I will be asking for some help on completing the latter. I think if I lay out new things I want to try or do in a bullet point unordered format I could get some people to join me in new endeavors. Writing it is a big step though. The three point oh thing will be discussed here another day. But it'll take a lot of magical focus and intentionality to achieve. I believe in myself to make a list. There are certainly some disadvantages to adding structure to my life, but it's better than watching the clock spin while I do this:[cow thinking about eating grass].

title: ty mr greep
body: The New Sound is one of those records that produced a vivid memory the first time I heard it, one that I can't shake whenever I return to it. In my car, stuck in 5 o'clock traffic right next to the Walker's sculpture garden, I heard Geordie Greep's impassioned howling on the album's second track Terra. The thought struck me, 'Oh, I'm going to love this'. I hadn't been a black midi regular, so it was certainly new territory for me. Heightened by the Latin drums and labyrinthian lyrics I descended into the madness and resulting clarity of Greep's (astoundingly) first solo project. Later that year it was set in stone by a live show I saw at First Avenue which was easily one of my favorites of all time. In one word, intrusive. The New Sound presents a stylization of an internal monologue, thoughts that verge on rational but step over the line, only to salsa back into normality. The album is profoundly relatable at time and at others fiercely alien, but only for a fleeting verse. The music itself is from another dimension as well, one slightly askew with broad influences and narrow performances. The spotlight is shone on Greep throughout, sometimes softly lighting its subject, sometimes so bright his flesh begins to boil, sometimes both in the same track. The chief accomplishment of this dichotomy.. you can't look away.

title: doing too much
body:
truthfully, many things are far more unique than we give them credit for. obscured by the human instinct of comparison and metaphor, the persistent digging for a connection to aid in understanding is reductive. we cannot be blamed for the habit, it is effective to our pursuit of gathering knowledge. that said, comparison is an obstacle to discovering the true essence of a thing. it is not a foot in the door but a kick through the door, forever burdening something pure and all alone itself with the yoke of category.

this shortcoming is surely a symptom of the neural pathways being just that, pathways. to me it lends credence to the theory that the human mind is not capable of understanding itself. and it may be for good reason that it cannot.

title: the genius killer
body: In 2023 I was listening to Wednesday's Rat Saw God, a standout folky-punk record that typified my rotation at that time. I remember sharing it with my roommate who was later referenced it as 'That one with the song where she rambles about someone ODing over some guitars'. Yeah that's the one. Anyway, I can't remember when exactly, I would assume pretty quickly after the release of Lenderman's breakout Manning Fireworks I learned that this song, How Do You Let the Love Into the Heart That Isn't Split Wide Open was written and preformed by members of Wednesday. It had been nestled up in my spotify for years after it was recommended to me, and I returned regularly to this distortion drenched poem that always felt like it had more to say than it said. That was the genesis of my MJ Lenderman fandom, which has marched forward and even expanded my tastes into more southern rock inspired indie in the 2020's. Love this song. Love the concept of the title being the lyrics. It's the best way you can spend 63 seconds. Now you can love it too.

title: on totep
body: TOTEP was the genesis of this site and I've been meaning to write about it since the site went live. I am not entirely sure of the form these music posts will take. For now, I just want these to be a little blurb about what an album makes me think of or how it makes me feel. If nothing else, it will exist as a time capsule and a bastion of genuine human opinion on the web as the dead internet closes in. TOTEP is a 2018 EP from British pop trio Kero Kero Bonito. Landing months before their second studio album Time 'n' Place, it is the first published collection of KKB songs that saw a thorough departure from their bubblegum J-pop style that typified their breakout releases. Despite much thought in the last few weeks, I haven't been able to pin down what exactly about this project made it such a north star for my personal site and my blogging. Today I'm beginning to grasp it. Sometimes you just need to try something, and it doesn't need to be a complete thought, just capturing an impulse is valuable and creatively rich. To me, the glitchy and noisy direction of this EP strikes the perfect balance of catchy, soaring progressions with distorted riffs and heavy breakdowns. The hooks are still immaculate but the bouncy refrains of Bonito Generation are traded in for storytelling and emotional imagery that is as distorted as the backing. Only Acting will forever be the standout, and was the only track here that was pulled into the coming LP. A microcosm of the KKB journey, a cutesy hook is the nail on which the driving instrumental is draped preceding a total glitch breakdown and the most iconic high-energy KKB moment until a concert video of them covering Death Grips' I've Seen Footage popped up online. Classic. The test post on this site contains Cinema, a personal favorite. Dreamy and listless, Cinema captures a wandering feeling that is somewhat vacant on the tight, rhythmic projects that precede it. Anyway, I love this little thing. It's rare to get a look inside the moment an artist pivots their sound, to see the unrefined moment where they experiment with something new and sound great doing it. As I stared at TOTEP in the record store, tucked between the physically larger albums on the rack, its aesthetic and the credo I had ascribed to it called to me. And now it's on my shelf.

title: i'm fine now
body:
I'm dissociating again. I know how to deal with this. Was this the common denominator? Was this always the real problem? I was wound up like this every day it's no wonder I was drowning this feeling. I didn't know what life was like without it. To me, knowing that I could go back on  the medication and the physical symptoms of anxiety would cease was a tool in my anti-anxiety kit. Could the same be true for these stimulants? Is knowing that I can live and succeed and be happy without them enough to help me separate out the benefits and deal with the consequences. Why did I decide to change my life by taking meds? I mean, the question has answered itself with the amount of work I've done in a half hour. I've written more in the last twenty minutes that I have in weeks. But is any of this real or publishable or usable? Can I bare this part of my life for others?

I've touched a bit on why I feel protected posting personal things on this site. I'm not remarkable. But there's another part of this, my emotional thrill-seeking and recent habit of battering my own heart to ensure that I have one. It may never be posted here, but I recently wrote about over-exposing my self to heartbreak in order to feel something profound. My lack of ability to feel torn asunder by the world creates a feeling of twisted FOMO. I think it could be ascribed to my unique way of processing grief. Perhaps the resilience, or alternatively, the callousness I've gained through reconstructing my life anew has left me distant to my surroundings. It's not that I don't have deep empathy and grief and sorrow and joy and bliss. It just rarely overwhelms me. Maybe my over consumption of media, and that media's obsession with catastrophe and extraordinary circumstance that defines character has reenforced this shell. Life just isn't like that.

That must be why I threw this wrench into my life. To saturate my days with life lived and thoughts expressed. To feel generative. Deep down I hope this place has a purpose. That baring my soul teaches me something about myself. My gaseous thought splattered onto a digital canvas.
rating: -ryan wrote this to quell a panic attack

title: go dogs
body: It's an odd feeling. Not different necessarily, not distorted. I can just focus now, I can write or code or send an email without my eyes darting from monitor to monitor. I'm able to clearly process in a way I just couldn't for, what, 6 years now? I picture my head filled with gaseous particles bouncing off my skull, creating an equilibrium with the outside world, scattered and pinballing around. Then they slow down just enough to form some order, some pattern in the chaos. The point between my eyes where I often feel a thread pulling me is now an aperture for my gaseous thought. The bridge of my nose a vector of my intention, like a bloodhound following a scent.  I was clearly dependent when I quit. I've worked hard for in the time since I've stopped taking the stuff to learn to live without it. But now, I'm plugged in again. Plodding away, vision narrowed. I'm not sure this is how it's supposed to be. Is this what other people feel like? Is this okay? Is it worth the strife and anxiety? Is all this self imposed? A placebo effect and a placebo side effect? Even the questions flow through my brain in a neat stream and that unsettles me.

title: "don't post anything you wouldn't want read at your funeral"
body: I'm about to post some things that I may or may not want read at my funeral. This wisdom comes to us from an era when anonymity and permanence were central to web culture. Recently, I feel these principals slipping away. My job, address, and contact info are all available publicly online. My handful of emails addresses and their sprawling web of connected accounts trace all my online activity back to me. My DNA is in the hands of a corporation who will now sell it to the highest bidder thanks to a spit-vial birthday present I received at age 15. Anonymity is dead. And I think permanence will be soon to follow. This post was inspired by The Internet Is Full Of Ghosts, a MLYP video about the digital footprint of people who have passed away. In my opinion, this video properly depicts the trash heap that the web has become. So here I want to justify shoveling something valuable onto the heap. It will be buried. If ever there was media to become lost, it's my personal anecdotes on my silly website with my name on it. Even still, my words are intentional and made from a human keystroke on a keyboard, which is more than can be said for the majority of the internet. And if it does get discovered or mined or used against me so be it. As I will make clear on this page, I crave a little anguish now and then. One day, this site will be a time capsule of however long I bothered to update it. And then it will go down when I stop paying for the web address of my name. And then one day the wayback machine will be deprecated and the words will drift onward. If this sounds too poetic, good, it feels like the proper way to justify spilling my heart here. So read this is at my funeral.

title: this place
body: For as long as I can remember, I've made a habit of walking into a store and filling an imaginary cart with a few things I'd like to buy, genuinely considering a purchase, and strolling out empty handed. Often it will take me 2, 3, maybe even more trips to commit to buying something I don't need. Nowhere is this more apparent than the record store, where I can never seem to justify the haul that piles up in my head as I pace the isles, thumbing through records for the occasional dopamine release: "Ooh, I love this one!". Recently I found myself in the same routine. Yet while holding TOTEP, and over the following days another thought arose that would become the seed of this space. Indecision, commitment, and perfectionism are all themes that may rear their heads here but they also represent the foundation on which this exercise was built. What if I forced myself to write down my passing thoughts and throw them at the wall? What if I forced myself to trust the instinct, to protect myself from the overthinking and analysis of my opinion that paralyzes me? So here we are, on ryanfeb.us, the blog/wall/review space that proposes a solution. I buy records. I write about that. I experience life. I write about that. Other things happen. I write about that. It's open-ended, low commitment fun for the whole family. Actually just for me and you. I imagine if I do commit to writing regularly here that this glossy buttoned-up style will devolve into something resembling how I actually speak with people. Retaining some weight in the thoughts I'm expressing while being true to my current 'guy who is never offline' voice may be the initial balancing act. I've thought about the tenor of the content I'll share here as well; I've considered how truly unfiltered I want to be. The levies against my fear of over-exposing my thoughts here are twofold. One, I'd like to drown this page in unedited writing and will be creating mostly chaff until I can write wheat. (Is that how wheat works? Like, when you're bad at growing wheat is there more chaff?) Anyway, the other levy is the nature of hosting a blog on my personal website with a bunch of my opinions on it. I'm wholly unremarkable when viewed from thirty-thousand feet, and my webpage should be no different. If you're reading this, thank you. You're staring at the anthill, observing one ant's every move. I'm imposing no structure on this page but I am stating some goals up top. A weekly post or addition to the site. Become more comfortable with expressing myself imperfectly. Buy some records. And exhale one percent deeper from offloading some of the thoughts I carry onto this page. In the short term, begin to roll the snowball downhill and mask the imperfections with growth and speed.
